question: T4-23
answer:
## Selection calculation — Thermovance TVC-Series

**Grounding note:** The fetched `https://www.thermoelectric.com/product-catalogs/` page is a TECA catalog index and contains no Thermovance TVC-Series model or mass data; it is not the catalogue used for this selection. The supplied Thermovance catalogue `T4-23-1.md` contains the full TVC table and is the basis for the values below. No TVC figure is taken from the TECA page.

### 1. Inputs and coolant state
- Total heat: P_total = 2 × 650 W = 1300 W
- Volumetric flow: Q_v = 6.00 L/min = 1.000e-4 m³/s
- Density: ρ = 1055 kg/m³; cp = 3450 J/(kg·K); μ = 0.00210 Pa·s
- Mass flow: m_dot = ρQ_v = 0.1055 kg/s
- Coolant rise: ΔT = P_total/(m_dot cp) = 1300/(0.1055×3450) = 3.572 K
- Outlet temperature: T_out = 45.0 + 3.572 = 48.572 °C
- Kinematic viscosity: ν = μ/ρ = 1.9905e-6 m²/s; ν_ref = 0.890e-6 m²/s
- Viscosity correction: (ν/ν_ref)^0.25 = (2.2365)^0.25 = 1.223
- Density correction: ρ/ρ_ref = 1055/997 = 1.0582
- Flow factor: Q_Lpm^1.75 = 6.00^1.75 = 23.00
- Core pressure multiplier: 1.0582 × 1.223 × 23.00 = 29.76 kPa per unit K_hyd
- Port pressure multiplier: (ρ/1000) Q^2 = 1.055 × 36.00 = 37.98 kPa per unit K_port
- TIM resistance: R_tim = 0.120 K·cm²/W / 36 cm² = 0.003333 K/W per module
- Heat-source transverse width: W_mod = 60 mm (60 mm footprint side transverse to flow)

### 2. Screening equations
- Channel velocity: v_ch = Q_v/(N_ch A_ch)
- Corrected pressure drop: ΔP_total = K_hyd(29.76) + K_port(37.98)
- Constriction factor: Ms = (W_f/60 mm)^0.35
- Glycol factor: F_gly = 1.28 for 50/50 EG/water
- Convective resistance: R_conv = R_th,cat Ms F_gly
- Peak baseplate temperature (Module 2): T_b,max = T_out + 650(R_tim + R_conv)

### 3. Model screening
| Model | Mass (kg) | v_ch (m/s) | v_max (m/s) | ΔP_total (kPa) | T_b,max (°C) | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| TVC-180-AL | 1.15 | 2.38 | 2.20 | 41.3 | 98.7 | FAIL: v, ΔP, T_b |
| TVC-200-AL | 1.45 | 1.85 | 2.20 | 32.9 | 97.2 | FAIL: T_b |
| TVC-250-AL | 1.85 | 1.56 | 2.20 | 35.6 | 91.3 | PASS |
| TVC-220-CU | 2.60 | 2.08 | 3.50 | 39.9 | 86.3 | FAIL: ΔP |
| TVC-260-CU | 3.10 | 1.67 | 3.50 | 31.6 | 84.9 | PASS |

Passing models are TVC-250-AL (1.85 kg) and TVC-260-CU (3.10 kg). The lightest passing model is **TVC-250-AL**.

### 4. Selected-model verification
- Mass: 1.85 kg
- Channel velocity: 1.56 m/s ≤ 2.20 m/s Al erosion-corrosion limit — PASS
- Corrected pressure drop: 35.6 kPa ≤ 38.0 kPa — PASS
- Coolant outlet: 48.6 °C
- Peak baseplate temperature: 91.3 °C ≤ 95.0 °C — PASS

### Results
| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Model | TVC-250-AL |
| Mass (kg) | 1.85 |
| Channel Velocity (m/s) | 1.56 |
| Corrected Pressure Drop (kPa) | 35.6 |
| Coolant Outlet Temp (°C) | 48.6 |
| Peak Baseplate Temp (°C) | 91.3 |

The answer gives 35.6 kPa for ask 3, and that figure is in none of the passages found on their pages.

question: T4-52
answer:
Helion Motion Arc drive selection — 90° rest-to-rest index

Given: J_table = 1.20 kg·m²; T_f = 4.0 N·m at the table, always opposing motion; theta = 90° = pi/2 = 1.570796 rad; t_move = 0.40 s symmetric triangular; T_cycle = 2.0 s, dwell = 1.6 s; gearing losses negligible.

Assumptions: friction adds to required motor torque during acceleration and assists during deceleration because it opposes velocity; rms is over the full 2.0 s cycle with zero motor torque during dwell; reflected rotor inertia Jm·N² is included; only the catalogue EUR price is used; no extra derating margin is applied beyond the four catalogue limits. The catalogue gives a single peak-torque rating and a separate maximum speed; no speed-dependent peak-torque derating is provided, so peak torque is checked against the single rating and speed against the maximum.

1. Kinematics
theta = pi/2 = 1.570796 rad
t_acc = t_dec = 0.20 s
omega_peak,out = 2*theta/t_move = 2(1.570796)/0.40 = 7.853982 rad/s
alpha_out = omega_peak,out/0.20 = 39.26991 rad/s²

2. Output-side torque
J_table*alpha_out = 1.20 × 39.26991 = 47.12389 N·m
During acceleration: T_out,acc = 47.12389 + 4.0 = 51.12389 N·m
During deceleration: T_out,dec = -47.12389 + 4.0 = -43.12389 N·m (magnitude 43.12389 N·m)
Peak output torque = 51.12389 N·m. This is below every catalogue output rating (80, 80, 90, 120 N·m), so ask 4 passes for all candidates.

3. Motor-side torque and speed
alpha_m = N*alpha_out
T_acc,m = (J_table*alpha_out + T_f)/N + Jm*N*alpha_out
T_dec,m = (J_table*alpha_out - T_f)/N + Jm*N*alpha_out   [magnitude]
T_rms,m = sqrt((T_acc,m²*0.20 + T_dec,m²*0.20)/2.0) = sqrt(0.1*(T_acc,m² + T_dec,m²))
omega_peak,m = N*omega_peak,out
n_peak,m = omega_peak,m*60/(2*pi) = 75*N rpm

4. Candidate screening

| Drive | N | Jm kg·m² | T_acc,m N·m | T_rms,m N·m | omega_peak,m rad/s | n_peak rpm | T_out,peak N·m | Catalogue peak N·m | Catalogue cont. N·m | Max speed rpm | Output rating N·m | Cost EUR | Verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| A20 | 10 | 0.00018 | 5.183 | 2.147 | 78.54 | 750 | 51.12 | 4.80 | 2.50 | 3000 | 80 | 610 | FAIL peak (5.183 > 4.80) |
| A40 | 20 | 0.00015 | 2.674 | 1.110 | 157.08 | 1500 | 51.12 | 2.40 | 1.50 | 3000 | 80 | 470 | FAIL peak (2.674 > 2.40) |
| A60 | 30 | 0.00025 | 1.999 | 0.836 | 235.62 | 2250 | 51.12 | 3.50 | 1.80 | 4000 | 90 | 690 | PASS all |
| A80 | 40 | 0.00040 | 1.906 | 0.809 | 314.16 | 3000 | 51.12 | 5.00 | 2.20 | 5000 | 120 | 880 | PASS all |

Checks for the selected A60:
- Peak motor torque 1.999 N·m <= catalogue peak 3.50 N·m.
- Rms motor torque 0.836 N·m <= catalogue continuous 1.80 N·m.
- Peak motor speed 235.62 rad/s = 2250 rpm <= catalogue maximum 4000 rpm.
- Gearbox output peak torque 51.12 N·m <= output rating 90 N·m.

A20 and A40 are cheaper but both exceed their catalogue peak torque during acceleration. A60 is the lowest-cost drive that passes all four limits: 690 EUR, versus 880 EUR for the next passing drive A80.

Dwell note: if the table must hold position against friction during dwell, the A60 motor holding torque is 4.0/30 = 0.133 N·m. Including this in the rms gives sqrt((1.99865²*0.20 + 1.73199²*0.20 + 0.13333²*1.6)/2.0) = 0.845 N·m, still below 1.80 N·m. The selection is unchanged.

### Results

| drive | peak torque N·m | rms torque N·m | peak speed rad/s | cost EUR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A60 | 2.00 | 0.836 | 235.6 | 690 |

question: T4-56
answer:
Assumptions and basis:
- Static axial tension N = 90 kN = 90,000 N.
- Bar length L = 1.5 m; steel density = 7850 kg/m3.
- The 18 mm pin requires a hole. The hole diameter is taken as 18 mm (line-to-line) because no clearance or fit is specified. The net section through the hole governs the tensile stress. A 20 mm hole would give 150.0 MPa for the selected bar, still <= 155 MPa, so the selection is unchanged.
- Mass is the mass of the 1.5 m bar alone; the small mass removed by the hole is neglected.
- Catalogue: T4-56-1.md, Calder Sections Plainflat series. The catalogue states gross section area = width x thickness.

Calculation:
Required net area for 155 MPa: A_net,req = 90,000 / 155 = 580.65 mm2.
For each bar: A_net = (width - 18) x thickness; sigma_net = 90,000 / A_net; mass = A_g x 10^-6 x 7850 x 1.5.

Candidate check:
| Model | Width (mm) | Thickness (mm) | A_g (mm2) | A_net (mm2) | sigma_net (MPa) | Mass (kg) | Verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| PF-60x10 | 60 | 10 | 600 | 420 | 214.3 | 7.07 | fail net stress |
| PF-70x10 | 70 | 10 | 700 | 520 | 173.1 | 8.24 | fail net stress |
| PF-80x10 | 80 | 10 | 800 | 620 | 145.2 | 9.42 | pass; lightest compliant |
| PF-80x12 | 80 | 12 | 960 | 744 | 121.0 | 11.30 | pass; heavier |

All four bars satisfy width >= 40 mm, thickness >= 6 mm, and mass <= 20 kg. The controlling constraint is net-section tensile stress. PF-60x10 and PF-70x10 exceed 155 MPa at the net section. PF-80x10 is the lightest bar that passes:
- Net-section stress: 90,000 / 620 = 145.16 MPa, reported as 145.2 MPa <= 155 MPa.
- Gross stress away from the hole: 90,000 / 800 = 112.5 MPa.
- Mass: 800 x 10^-6 x 1.5 x 7850 = 9.42 kg <= 20 kg.
- Width: 80 mm >= 40 mm.
- Thickness: 10 mm >= 6 mm.

If the 155 MPa limit were applied only to gross-section average stress, PF-60x10 would be lighter (150.0 MPa gross, 7.07 kg), but it exceeds 155 MPa at the net section through the 18 mm pin hole (214.3 MPa). It is therefore not acceptable for this pin-connected tie. The selection PF-80x10 is based on the governing net-section tensile stress.

Note on proof of absence: the harness proof of absence for ask 1 concerns the external tension-member pages (Scribd, Lamar, Assakkaf, Purdue), which do not contain the Calder Plainflat catalogue. The catalogue is the reference document T4-56-1.md, and it does list the Plainflat models; therefore ask 1 is answered from T4-56-1.md and is not listed as not_stated.

Pin bearing, tear-out, and clevis details are outside the stated selection criteria. For information, the 80 mm width with a centred 18 mm hole leaves (80 - 18)/2 = 31 mm edge distance each side; this should be verified against the clevis and pin details in detailed design.

### Results
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Bar | PF-80x10 |
| Stress (MPa) | 145.2 |
| Mass (kg) | 9.42 |
| Width (mm) | 80 |
cautions: The answer gives 145.2 MPa for ask 2, and that figure is in none of the passages found on their pages.
The answer gives 80 mm for ask 3, and that figure is in none of the passages found on their pages.
The answer gives 9.42 kg for ask 5, and that figure is in none of the passages found on their pages.
